summary.one_liner: Docker image and compose setup for Pi-hole, a network-wide DNS-based ad blocker that runs on your own Linux hardware.
summary.what_it_does: The README provides a Docker Compose example for running the pihole/pihole image, mapping DNS (53 TCP/UDP), HTTP (80) and HTTPS (443) ports, with optional DHCP (67/udp) and NTP (123/udp) ports. Configuration is done through environment variables such as TZ, the web interface password (FTLCONF_webserver_api_password) and the DNS listening mode (FTLCONF_dns_listeningMode). Volumes persist Pi-hole's databases and config in /etc/pihole, with an optional dnsmasq.d mount for custom dnsmasq files. Optional capabilities (NET_ADMIN, SYS_TIME, SYS_NICE) are added for DHCP, NTP and process priority. The container runs cron to refresh ad lists weekly and flush logs. Image tags include latest, date-based releases, and nightly builds from the development branch.
use_cases: Block ads and trackers across every device on a home network
Run Pi-hole as a DHCP server in Docker
Self-host a DNS sink or ad-blocking resolver on a Linux box
how_to_run: Copy the docker-compose example from the README and adjust the timezone, password and volumes
Run: docker compose up -d (or docker-compose on older systems)
notable: Optional DHCP and NTP server ports, enabled by uncommenting lines
Weekly automatic ad list updates via cron built into the container
Nightly image tag built from the development branch
caveats: The README advises against using the --privileged flag on 2022.04 and later, and recommends explicit capabilities instead
Using Docker's default bridge network requires setting the DNS listening mode to ALL
Watchtower users are directed to a separate note in the documentation
